END QUOTED DATA` (an embedded end marker is neutralised), then removed before compiling; they never reach the jar, the source zip or shared knowledge. An imported workspace keeps a narrower allow-list after every model turn (Java sources, data resources, `modbuilder.json`, the template); anything else the model writes is removed and reported as a rejected change (`rejectedPaths`), and every output still passes compile + the attested scan with the baseline.
144	
145	**Portal flow** (`importMod`): attestation check -> idempotency (same bytes from the same account return the existing import, re-quarantined if it was deleted; found by `engine.import.uploadSha256`) -> **quarantine the raw bytes first** -> ingest -> attestation record with detected licences -> `createProject` (reserves the `nx_` namespace for NEW identifiers; existing names are never renamed) -> the root revision (the plan's "revision 0"; the store numbers it seq 1, no parent), kind `imported`, ModSpec v1 derived from the descriptor (summary, one requirement per command, compile/scan tests), file manifest with sha256 + roles, the import record -> source: a ModBuild row (`prompt: "Imported plugin: <name>"`, `rootBuildId` = itself, and the project's `rootBuildId` = it, so the change flow, assets and projects UI find it) + the service base build; jar: the service analysis job; packs: passed at once. `getImport` syncs the service and settles the revision once (passed / failed). `deleteImport` removes the quarantined bytes; the project and its append-only history (hashes + attestation) stay. `checkImportConflicts` runs the inventory + conflict engine for an imported plugin against one of the user's servers (read-only; the uploaded jar, or the import's built jar once ready). API gates in order: flag (404) -> signed-in Cyrus user (404) -> verified email (403) -> rate limits (2/min, 10/h, 30/day per account; 6/min for conflict checks) -> running builds/imports cap (2) -> size caps (413) -> type/version checks.
146	
147	**Tests (RAN on node-2 via devhost)**: `cyrus-import.test.ts` 85 + `cyrus-import-api.test.ts` 10 + `modbuilder-import-pipeline.test.ts` 7 + `cyrus-import-db.test.ts` 5 (throwaway DB), all passing; the existing pipeline, scan, inventory, engine-core, conflicts, modpack, assets, sounds, efficiency and live suites still pass (418 together). `tsc` clean. `test/cyrus-admin.test.ts` fails the same way on the base branch (a server-only import), unrelated.
148	
149	**REAL runs on node-2** (`scripts/devhost run --lock -- npx tsx test/cyrus-import-real.ts`; raw results `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/import-r2-real-2026-10-10.json`). No real game client and no AI model were used (the import path makes no model call). The four allowlist jars re-verified (sha256 + sha1 + size). The REAL `services/modbuilder/server.js` ran on node-2 with JDK 21 (Test Flight's Temurin 21.0.12.1) and, for 26.2, JDK 25 (a test-only registry copy marked 26.2 buildable; the shipped registry still says preview), the resolved Paper classpaths, the allowlisted jars, and `yaml@2.8.1` installed into `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-import-real/svcdeps` (npm sha512 integrity matched the registry). The fixture project (`test/fixtures/cyrus-import/demo-src`: Vault economy hook, PlaceholderAPI expansion, a bStats-style HTTPS metrics class, a Spigot update checker, a command with a reload subcommand, a join listener, config.yml, a Gradle build with a malicious `steal` task, gradlew, a README with a prompt-injection comment, an MIT LICENSE) went through the portal ingestion (build files dropped, deps = placeholderapi + vault-api) and `POST /imports`:
150	- 1.21.11: succeeded in 1.7 s; `Checked with the attested profile: 5 warnings` (reflection-lookup and network-http in Metrics, network-http in UpdateChecker, two network-endpoint), **no blocks**; jar 10,250 bytes, class major 65, no shaded dependency classes, no build files, the author's plugin.yml comment kept; the same import again gave the same jar sha256 (reproducible).
151	- 26.2: succeeded in 1.6 s with the same 5 warnings; class major 69; reproducible.
152	- `evil-src` (Runtime.exec from a command): failed `safety`, `block:exec@me.demo.evil.EvilImport`.
153	- Test Flight (one at a time; node-2 was busy with another agent's flight three times and the backoff waited): 1.21.11 **passed** (boot 18.1 s; plugins enabled, startup log clean, `/plugins` lists ImportDemo, `/importdemo` and `/importdemo reload` answer, clean stop, no leaks); 26.2 **passed** with the 26.2 build (boot 11.0 s, same 6 checks).
154	
155	**Design decisions the plan did not specify**: the root revision is seq 1 (the store's numbering) and is what the plan calls revision 0; jar-only and pack imports have no ModBuild row (they cannot be changed, so nothing would use one); import compile errors fail the import with the compiler output (no AI repair at import; ask Cyrus after importing a version that compiles); raw sockets, JarFile and encoded blobs stay blocked even for owned code; bStats is refused as a dependency (must be shaded) but its copied-in source is fine; build-file-only dependencies are notes, imports are what count; idempotency is by upload hash per account and is sequential (two simultaneous identical uploads could still make two projects; the per-minute limit makes it rare); `deleteImport` keeps the history; the conflict check replaces an older copy of the same plugin on the server rather than reporting it as a clash.
156	
157	**Owner actions / decisions**: (1) review the attestation and share-consent wording (bump the version constants when changed); (2) rate limits and the 25 MB cap; (3) enabling `cyrus_import_enabled` (only after the build-service image has `import.js`, `deps.json` + the verified jars in `/opt/mb/deps` and the deploy); (4) the VM image change: copy `lib/cyrus/import/deps.json` next to the Dockerfile and rebuild (the image build fetches and verifies the jars; the Dockerfile's app COPY line also still lacks the R1 `textures.js`/`sounds.js` files, check before rebuilding); (5) which further dependencies to allowlist; (6) whether GPL dependencies (PlaceholderAPI, ProtocolLib) need a note to users about their own plugin's licence; (7) quarantine retention (nothing expires uploads yet).

content.content:
1	## Cyrus data pack studio (R2)
2	
3	Branch `feature/cyrus-r4` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 2b, 4.3, 4.11, R2 days 13-14; research `A2-datapacks.md`. **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** Two flags, both OFF by default (fail closed): `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO=1` (portal: the build request may get the data pack route) and `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL=1` (worker: a built data pack may be placed on a server). Off, every build request is byte-identical to before and no code touches a server. Data packs are **not plan-gated** (owner decision for composition features): no plan lookup happens for them. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports (the delivery uses the existing `MemberPlacer` from `lib/cyrus/modpack/install.ts`), no new tables, no foreign keys; assets go into the existing `CyrusProjectAsset` table with `kind = "datapack"`.
4	
5	**The flow.** Request -> capability router (data-driven words) -> the build service's AI writes **typed spec files** `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (never raw Minecraft JSON) -> the service validates + emits them with the GENERATED copy of the TypeScript code for the build's exact version, bounded repairs, drop-not-ship -> the portal re-validates and re-emits (the service is not trusted), records a revision + a datapack asset -> (flag) delivery into `<level>/datapacks/` + `minecraft:reload` (or a restart for enchantments).
6	
7	### 1. Files (`lib/cyrus/datapack/`)
8	| File | What |
9	|---|---|
10	| `spec.ts` | DataPackSpec v1 (Zod) + `validateDataPackSpec(json, { version, namespace })` -> `{ ok, spec, errors, warnings, checks }` (never throws) + `canonicalJson` + `needsRestart` |
11	| `datapack.v1.schema.json` | the portable contract (JSON Schema), generated (see below; a test fails while stale) |
12	| `versions.ts` | `dataPackFeatures(version)` (the verified per-version differences, below), `vanillaIds(kind, version)`, `isVanilla`, `missingIdReason` ("needs 1.21.11 or newer" / "was removed after 1.21.8") |
13	| `data/vanilla-ids.json` | ids ONLY (238 KB): items, blocks, entity types, enchantments, loot tables, advancements, recipes, item/block/entity/enchantment tags, loot function / condition / entry / number types, triggers, recipe serializers, enchantment effect components, mob effects, attributes, command roots, execute sub-commands, gamerules; grouped by a version bitmask. Generated by Mojang's data generator (`--reports --server`) from each pinned vanilla server jar on node-2 (sha256s in the file's `source`). No assets or content |
14	| `data/mcdoc-subset.json` | field tables derived from **vanilla-mcdoc** (SpyglassMC, MIT, commit `1528808766ccaaac10e64de002b05d3efc31a9a3`, attribution in the file): top-level keys, optional flags and `since`/`until` of every struct the emitters write |
15	| `mcdoc.ts` | resolves those tables per version (`dispatchFields`, `structFields`, `checkKeys`); outside the subset = null = not judged |
16	| `functions.ts` | the function SAFETY validator (allowlist, below) |
17	| `emit/{common,recipe,loot,advancement,enchantment,index}.ts` | per-version emitters; `buildDataPack(spec, ctx)` = validate -> emit -> static file check -> deterministic zip (`lib/cyrus/textures/zip.ts`: sorted entries, fixed timestamps) -> `{ zip, sha1, sha256, files, counts, apply: reload|restart, checks }` |
18	| `validate.ts` | `validatePackFiles(files, version)`: the static checker for emitted OR raw files (imports) |
19	| `route.ts` | `decideDataPackRoute` (build request), `routeWithDataPack` (router with the route switched on), `hasDatapacks`, flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO` |
20	| `sync.ts` | `checkReturnedDatapacks` (portal re-validation / re-emission, cross-pack duplicates) |
21	| `deliver.ts` | `planDataPackDelivery`, `rebuildForDelivery`, `deliverDataPack` (flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`) |
22	| `import.ts` | `importDataPackZip`, `exportImported`, `checkRawResource` (edit/import library) |
23	| `service-entry.ts` | esbuild entry of the service copy |
24	
25	Scripts: `scripts/cyrus/build-datapack-artifacts.ts [--check] [--out-dir DIR]` writes `services/modbuilder/datapack-spec.js` (bundled validator + emitter incl. zod and the id data, minified, 650 KB) and the JSON Schema; run it through `devhost run ... --out-dir /tank/nxeon-build/tmp/...` and copy back (devhost's next push deletes files written inside the node-2 copy). `scripts/cyrus/datapack-derive.py ids|mcdoc` re-derives the two data files on node-2 (see 8).
26	
27	### 2. DataPackSpec v1
28	`{ schemaVersion: 1, name, description, resources: [1-128] }`; `name` = file name. Every resource lives in the project's reserved namespace (`id` is only the path; engine-core identifiers gained the kind `resource` for `nx_x:a/b/c`, recipes use the existing `recipe` kind). References are full ids: own ones must exist in the spec, vanilla ones must exist in the TARGET version's id lists, any other namespace is refused.
29	- **recipe**: `shaped` (pattern 1-3 x 1-3, key), `shapeless` (1-9), `smelting` / `blasting` / `smoking` / `campfire_cooking` (experience, cookingTime), `stonecutting`, `smithing_transform`. Ingredient = id, `#tag` or a list of alternatives. Result = vanilla item + count + optional `name` (`minecraft:item_name`) and `lore` (a data pack cannot add items). Not supported: `smithing_trim`, special recipes, `crafting_transmute`.
30	- **loot_table**: kind generic/chest/entity/block/fishing/gift; pools (rolls = number / uniform / binomial, bonusRolls), entries item / tag (expand) / loot_table / empty with weight, quality; **functions subset**: set_count, set_damage, enchant_randomly, enchant_with_levels, set_name, set_lore, set_enchantments, explosion_decay, furnace_smelt, looting_bonus (= enchanted_count_increase with looting); **conditions subset**: random_chance, killed_by_player, survives_explosion, match_tool (items / tag), weather.
31	- **advancement**: parent (own or vanilla), display (icon, title, description, frame, background from the five vanilla tabs, toast/chat/hidden), **criteria subset**: impossible, tick, inventory_changed, consume_item, player_killed_entity, recipe_unlocked, recipe_crafted; requirements all|any; rewards experience / loot / recipes / function.
32	- **tag**: registry item / block / entity_type / function / enchantment; own tags, or additions to an EXISTING vanilla tag (`replace` defaults false; `replace: true` on a vanilla tag is refused); function tags: own, `minecraft:load`, `minecraft:tick`.
33	- **function**: a list of commands (+ `runOn: load|tick`, merged into the vanilla function tags).
34	- **enchantment**: description, supportedItems / primaryItems (tag or items), exclusiveSet, weight, maxLevel, min/max cost, anvil cost, slots, value effects (`damage`, `damage_protection`, `knockback`, `armor_effectiveness`, `item_damage`, `mob_experience`, `block_experience`, `repair_with_xp`, `smash_damage_per_fallen_block`; add / multiply / set, linear per level). Supported because the format of this subset was **verified identical on all six versions** (vanilla sharpness/unbreaking compared on every jar, and the custom enchantment loaded and was applied to an item on all six real servers). Enchantments are registry content: `apply = "restart"`.
35	- Not in v1: worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions: router warns; added in R4 behind `CYRUS_WORLDGEN`, see "Cyrus worldgen (R4)"), predicates / item modifiers as resources, vanilla loot-table or recipe overrides, macros.
36	
37	### 3. Per-version differences (VERIFIED on the real jars, 2026-10-10)
38	Method: the vanilla data generator of each pinned server jar dumped the vanilla data pack; the same files were compared across versions, cross-checked with vanilla-mcdoc, then the emitted packs were booted (section 6).
39	
40	| Difference | Versions | Evidence |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| Ingredients `{"item": id}` / `{"tag": id}` -> strings `"id"` / `"#tag"`; a list of alternatives may hold only item ids | 1.21.1 vs 1.21.2+ | vanilla `stick.json`, `fire_charge.json`, `netherite_sword_smithing.json`; mcdoc |
43	| Text in item components (`item_name`, `lore`) is a JSON **string** -> a text **object** | <=1.21.4 vs 1.21.5+ | vanilla `voluntary_exile.json` icon `minecraft:item_name` |
44	| Advancement background `minecraft:textures/gui/advancements/backgrounds/stone.png` -> `minecraft:gui/advancements/backgrounds/stone` | <=1.21.4 vs 1.21.5+ | vanilla `story/root.json` |
45	| `pack.mcmeta` `pack_format` -> `min_format` / `max_format` `[major, minor]` | <1.21.9 vs 1.21.9+ | mcdoc `pack.mcdoc`; registry formats 48 / 61 / 81 / 94.1 / 101.1 / 107.1 accepted by the real servers |
46	| Entity predicates `{"type": ...}` -> namespaced sub-predicates `{"minecraft:entity_type": ...}` | <26.2 vs 26.2 | vanilla `adventure/blowback.json`, `entities/zombie.json`; mcdoc `EntityPredicate` |
47	| Cooking results: single item (no count) -> item stack (count) | <26.1 vs 26.1+ | mcdoc `Smelting`; the validator refuses count > 1 before 26.1 |
48	| `smithing_transform.group` removed; `category` optional (26.2 vanilla drops it from many recipes) | 26.1+ / 26.2 | mcdoc; vanilla 26.2 recipes |
49	| Advancement icons: vanilla writes `count: 1` before 26.1, omits it after (both load; we mirror vanilla) | 26.1 | vanilla advancements |
50	| Loot `loot_table` entries reference by `value` (not `name`); tag entries need `expand` before 26.3 | all | mcdoc |
51	| Gamerules camelCase -> snake_case (`keepInventory` -> `keep_inventory`) | <=1.21.8 vs 1.21.11+ | `commands.json` of each jar |
52	| Item tag `#minecraft:enchantable/sword` removed, `#minecraft:enchantable/melee_weapon` added | 1.21.11 | vanilla tags (the validator caught it on the showcase) |
53	| Commands `rotate` (1.21.4+), `dialog`, `version`, `waypoint`, `test` (1.21.8+), `stopwatch`, `fetchprofile` (1.21.11+), `swing`, `unpublish` (26.x) | per version | `commands.json` |
54	
55	### 4. Validation (quality-bar style checks: pass / warn / fail / not_run)
56	Spec checks: `schema`, `namespace`, `vanilla_ids`, `references`, `version_features`, `limits`, `function_safety`. File checks on the emitted (or imported) files: `mcmeta`, `mcdoc_fields` (unknown / missing keys per version), `value_shapes` (the format changes above), `emitted_ids` (recipe types, loot function / condition / entry types, triggers, items), `emitted_functions`, `not_checked` (resources outside the subset: listed, kept, never judged). The same report is stored with every datapack asset.
57	
58	**Function allowlist** (`functions.ts`; functions run as the server at `function-permission-level`, 2 by default, up to 4 on some hosts). Allowed roots: advancement, attribute, bossbar, clear, clone, damage, data, dialog, effect, enchant, execute, experience/xp, fill, fillbiome, forceload, function, gamemode, gamerule, give, item, kill, list, locate, loot, me, msg/tell/w, particle, place, playsound, random, recipe, return, ride, rotate, say, schedule, scoreboard, setblock, spawnpoint, spectate, spreadplayers, stopsound, stopwatch, summon, swing, tag, team, teammsg/tm, teleport/tp, tellraw, time, title, trigger, waypoint, weather, worldborder; each must also exist in the target version's real command tree. Refused: op, deop, ban, ban-ip, banlist, pardon, pardon-ip, kick, whitelist, stop, save-off/on/all, reload, publish/unpublish, transfer, difficulty, defaultgamemode, setidletimeout, setworldspawn, seed, tick, debug, jfr, perf, test, fetchprofile, datapack, version, every namespaced root (`minecraft:op`, `bukkit:...`, plugin commands such as `lp`), macros (`$` lines, `function ... with`), `run_command` click actions, Command NBT, command / structure / jigsaw blocks, command-block minecarts and debug sticks anywhere, creative mode, `kill @e` without a type/tag/team/name/limit filter (`kill @a` warns), gamerules outside a gameplay list (both name styles). `execute ... run` and `return run` are unwrapped and checked to the end (nesting <= 12). Call graph over function / `execute if function` / function tags: no recursion, depth <= 8, calls only to this pack's own functions. Limits: 64 functions, 256 commands per function, 2048 commands and 256 KB per pack, 2000 chars per line, no line breaks, 64 commands per tick (tick functions and everything they call), 16 schedule commands (>= 1 tick, no `append` from tick functions), 4 `forceload add` (one chunk each). A summon in a tick function warns. Adversarial corpus: `test/fixtures/cyrus-datapack/function-corpus.json` (61 cases).
59	
60	### 5. Router, build service, portal
61	- **Router** (`adapters/minecraft.ts`, `engine-core/router.ts`): rules `datapack_recipe`, `datapack_loot`, `datapack_advancement`, `datapack_tag`, `datapack_function`, `datapack_enchantment`, `datapack_content` route to `dataPack` with limits (vanilla items only; function allowlist; enchantments need a restart; client-visible looks still need a resource pack); `worldgen` is now a `warn` ("not built yet; needs a restart"). The adapter keeps `dataPack` as `planned`; `RouteOptions.routesOn` lets the host switch a planned route on (`routeWithDataPack` does it under the flag), so `plugin+dataPack` becomes buildable only where enabled. "Creepers drop diamonds" stays a plugin (vanilla loot overrides are not in v1).
62	- **Build request** (`lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts`, one line in `lib/modbuilder/create.ts`): with the flag on, matched words, `assets: ["datapack"]` or a base build that has data packs give `service.assets.datapack = true` and a project namespace (no plan lookup); `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.datapack = { route, matched, limits }`; a version without an emitter (26.3) gets a notice and no route. Flag off: nothing decided, nothing recorded.
63	- **Build service** (`services/modbuilder/{datapacks.js,datapack-spec.js,datapack-example.json,prompts.js,server.js,textures.js}`): `assets.datapack` parsed (non-boolean = 400; switched off with a note where the bundle has no emitter for the version); the `DATA PACK` section is appended to the system prompt only when routed (fixed text, caches per version; the namespace is in the user turn); allow-list `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (max 4); a change build without the route keeps the base's specs byte for byte; every asset round runs `checkWorkspaceDatapacks` (the generated `buildDataPack` for the exact version + cross-file duplicates; HARD problems go back as `repair-asset`, bounded by `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS`, then the spec is dropped with a customer-visible limitation); `assetResult.datapacks: [{ name, path, sha256, spec, pack: { sha256, bytes, format, counts, apply, emitter }, checks, warnings }]`, `datapackPromptVersion` `mb-datapack-2026-10-10.1`; `/health` lists `datapack`. Data pack builds are never deduped. The service image needs the three new files.
64	- **Portal sync** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` + `datapack/sync.ts`): every returned spec is re-validated and re-emitted for `ModBuild.mcVersion`; failures and cross-pack duplicates are dropped; the same single revision of the build gets `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (role `asset`, spec sha256) and `datapack/<name>-<version>.zip` (role `dataPack`, zip sha256); one `CyrusProjectAsset` per pack (`kind datapack`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.datapack-spec+json`, provenance = spec, version, format, pack sha256/sha1, counts, apply, checks, `serviceAgreed`); `MbAssets.datapacks`. Idempotent (revision by modBuildId, content-addressed assets). **No hosting**: data packs never go to clients, and the emitter is deterministic, so delivery rebuilds the zip from the stored spec and checks the recorded sha256 (`rebuildForDelivery`); nothing is public.
65	- **Delivery** (`datapack/deliver.ts`, flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`): one file `<level>/datapacks/nxeon-<namespace>-<name>.zip` placed through a `MemberPlacer` (production: `engineMemberPlacer`, the Mods engine, staged writes, state file), then `minecraft:reload` over the console for reloadable content, or `restartRequired` for enchantments. **Remaining steps (not wired)**: (1) a worker job after the jar install that loads the build's datapack assets, `rebuildForDelivery`, and calls `deliverDataPack` with `engineMemberPlacer` + the server's level name + an RCON/console `runConsole`; (2) removal = the placer's `remove` + reload when a mod is uninstalled; (3) the NxLabs page line; (4) a real-server check of `minecraft:reload` discovering a NEW pack file (Test Flight reserves `reload`; boot discovery and `datapack disable/enable` were verified).
66

109	
110	**Scope (decided).** Vanilla data packs cannot safely edit the existing overworld biome mix, so Cyrus world generation lives in the mod's OWN namespace: (1) a custom **dimension** (`dimension_type` + `dimension`, noise generator from a vanilla terrain preset or a superflat generator) whose biome source (`fixed` / `checkerboard` / `multi_noise`) uses only the pack's own biomes; (2) custom **biomes** (climate, colours, music / ambience / particles, natural spawns, features, vanilla carvers); (3) **features** in those biomes (configured + placed: ores, oak-shaped trees, plant patches, lakes, single blocks; vanilla placed features may be listed too); (4) **structures**: block-layout templates compiled deterministically into `.nbt`, placed as single-piece jigsaw structures with `random_spread` structure sets, only in the pack's own biomes.
111	
112	**Honest limits (shown on the route, in the prompt, in the delivery plan).** World generation loads only when the server starts (Nxeon restarts once after install; `/reload` is not enough); it only shapes NEW chunks; the dimension is reached by the plugin's teleport command or `/execute in <ns>:<dim> run tp ...` (no portal), and it does not exist until that restart.
113	
114	**Not supported (documented, refused or warned):** editing the overworld / nether / end biomes or terrain; adding features or structures to vanilla biomes (biome modifiers are NeoForge/Fabric-only); merging worldgen from several packs (conflict engine: `datapack.worldgen_collision` / `datapack.worldgen_override`); custom noise settings, density functions, surface rules, carvers, multi-piece jigsaw; custom portals.

184	Chunk times are wall time from `forceload add` to all five probe positions loaded (poll every 250 ms + the per-step RCON time from runner tf-lite-3); node-2 is shared, so they are noisy (+-50%). Reading: two custom dimensions add 1.6-8.8 s to the FIRST boot (spawn preparation; older Paper builds pay most) and 0-180 MB RSS; the custom noise dimension (overworld terrain + the showcase features + ruins every ~8 chunks) generates at about 2x the vanilla nether (median ratio 2.1 over the six versions, i.e. about 130-400 ms per chunk on 2 cores), which matches the estimator (nether terrain 8 x 2.1 = ~17; showcase estimate 17.6 "low"); superflat is about 0.3x the nether (the estimator over-states flat dimensions with features: conservative). **Per-server recommendation** (`cost.recommendation`): low = any plan with 2 GB RAM or more; medium = 4 GB / 2 vCPU; high = 8 GB / 4 vCPU and pre-generate the dimension; above 100 refused.

All four together, 1.21.1 / 1.21.11 / 26.2: the real server **refuses to start** ("Registry loading errors ... Failed to load datapacks, can't proceed with server load", exit before Done) naming `Unknown registry key ... minecraft:random_patch`, `Spacing has to be larger than separation`, and on 1.21.1 `Not a JSON object: []` for the list-style carvers. Each file alone (26.2 and 1.21.1, 8 flights): the validator rejects all four on both versions; the server refuses to start for 7 of 8 and, on 26.2, BOOTS with the old-style biome (it tolerates int colours and ignores the moved keys: the sky / fog colours are silently lost), the silent break the validator exists to catch. **Consequence for delivery: a broken worldgen pack takes the whole server down at the next start**, so worldgen packs must only ever be delivered from a validated, re-emitted spec, and the delivery job needs a rollback (remove the pack and restart again if the server does not reach Done).
187

Nothing from the jars is stored in the repo.

192	### 7. Tests (RAN on devhost)
193	`test/cyrus-worldgen.test.ts` (62): feature matrix + block states; NBT round trips of every tag type, modified UTF-8, stored gzip vs real gunzip + CRC, the reader refusing truncated / trailing / bad tags / lengths / depth; template compiler read back (positions, palette order, void, loot nbt, block entities last, DataVersion only difference); showcase valid on all six versions, fail-closed without the route, R2 packs keep their report; an **adversarial corpus of 33 cases** (one mutation each, expected error code: own_only x3, unresolved_ref x3, foreign_namespace, unknown ids x6, own_block, denied blocks x2, block_state x2, separation, template shape / size / palette, noise_range, dimension_height, minY x16, flat_height, feature_order_cycle, not_spawnable, feature_attempts, biome_attempts, worldgen_count, worldgen_cost, unknown field); warnings; golden pack hashes per version (`test/fixtures/cyrus-worldgen/golden.json` = the flown packs); each verified difference in the emitted JSON; file validator on emitted files (all versions), the 1.21.4 files rejected for 26.2, the flown broken files, structure file defects, imports untouched; TS == generated JS (validation JSON and pack bytes on 14 inputs); service example on all versions; prompt section only when routed; router (off = R2, on, mixed, change keeps worldgen); build request; delivery; sync. `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` +3 (worldgen build through the fake CLI: section + restart pack, service bytes == TypeScript incl. NBT; the same spec without the route repaired twice then dropped; `assets.worldgen` validation). `test/cyrus-conflicts.test.ts` +4 mutations (two packs define the same dimension / the same custom biome = `worldgen_collision` blocking; the same vanilla biome overridden twice = `worldgen_override` blocking, once = warn). Also green: `test/cyrus-datapack.test.ts` 92 (R2 golden hashes unchanged), `test/cyrus-testflight.test.ts` 24. `tsc` clean.
194	
195	### 8. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
196	- Worldgen kinds are added to DataPackSpec **v1** (no schemaVersion bump): old specs stay valid and byte-identical; the switch is the validation context (`worldgen: true`), not the schema.
197	- Terrain shape only from vanilla noise presets (no custom noise / density functions): the main engine-safety decision.
198	- Structures are always single-piece jigsaw structures with a generated template pool (same id as the structure); no multi-piece jigsaw, no processors.
199	- `.` is the structure-void character; a stored gzip (no compression) for `.nbt` so bytes never depend on zlib; the outer zip compresses.
200	- Patches on 26.1+ are emitted the way vanilla 26.x does them (simple_block + count + random_offset + air filter on every placed feature that uses the patch).
201	- Custom end-like dimensions always get `has_ender_dragon_fight: false`; dimension types mirror vanilla's timeline tag per preset; `coordinateScale` defaults to 1.
202	- Natural spawns: a fixed allowlist of 55 mobs; denied blocks list (operator / technical / griefing blocks) applies to terrain, features and templates.
203	- Two packs defining the same worldgen id is **blocking** in the conflict engine (worldgen never stacks safely); one vanilla worldgen override is a warning.
204	- A change build of a mod whose pack has worldgen keeps the worldgen route (`existingWorldgen`), so later edits do not drop the dimension; if the flag is later turned off, the portal drops worldgen packs on sync (fail closed).
205	- Cost estimate is a documented heuristic calibrated against the node-2 flights, with a hard ceiling.

210	3. Wire the delivery job before `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL=1` for worldgen: restart (not reload), **rollback if the server does not reach Done after the restart** (a broken worldgen pack stops the server), and tell players the dimension exists only after that restart.
211	4. Decide what uninstalling a worldgen mod does with the generated dimension folders (`world_<ns>_<dim>` on 1.21.x, `world/dimensions/<ns>/<dim>` on 26.x): keep (default here, nothing deletes them) or archive.
212	5. Optional: confirm the natural-spawn allowlist, the denied-block list and the cost classes / recommendations.
213	6. Cleanup when no longer needed: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-datapack/r8` (derived data, 0.4 MB), `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-wg-*.json`, `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-r8-art`.

20809:- **Customer-chosen tier** (for the "Cyrus" UI): `POST /builds` accepts an optional `tier: "katara" | "saka" | "yakko"` (case-insensitive) or an explicit allowed `model`. It overrides routing, and no classifier call is made. Defaults: katara = `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, saka = `claude-sonnet-5`, yakko = `claude-opus-5` (`MB_TIER_KATARA/SAKA/YAKKO`). Opus 5.5 needs Claude Code ≥ 2.1.280, and the image has 2.1.241. Repairs stay on the chosen model and escalate one tier up only after two failed repairs. An unknown tier or model gets a 400. Recorded as `tier` and `override` in build.json. Requests without the field behave exactly as before.
20848:- **Knobs, off by default** (each needs an owner decision or an eval first): `MB_EFFORT=low|medium|high|xhigh|max` (same effort on every call of a build, since changing it mid-session throws the cache away; never sent to Haiku); `MB_CACHE_TTL=5m|1h` (`FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` / `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` for the CLI; 5m saves ~12% per build only when the same version + model builds more than about 15 times an hour, below that the 1 h default is cheaper; if the service moves to an API key, check `/health` and the spend split, and set `1h` explicitly if the CLI's default changes); `MB_DEDUPE=on` (an identical fresh, image-free request with the same version, plugin name, tier/model, prompt and knowledge version reuses the earlier build's source: copied, re-validated, re-compiled and re-scanned, no AI call, `costUsd` 0, so 0 Cyrus tokens; `"fresh": true` on `POST /builds` opts out; `MB_DEDUPE_MAX_AGE_H` default 168). `dedupeKey` is recorded on every eligible build either way, so the real repeat rate can be measured first.
20871:**UI.** `CyrusApp` (orchestration, polling, toasts, shortcuts, region measuring), `Dock` (glyph column + library drawer: search, Building / Favourites / All), `Home` (bottom console: headline, composer, template chips + template library), `Project` (strip with title / favourite / status / version / model / Install / Download / menu, older-version pill, inspector with **Live code / Explain / Versions / Notes**, change composer, focus mode `D`), `ProjectCaption` (pinned under the weave: stage headline, elapsed, last thoughts; outcome line; failure verdict with Try again / Edit and retry), `LiveCode` + `useLive` (polls `/live` with draft/seq/from, files appear the moment they land, the draft types itself out at the speed the AI writes it, edited lines glow once, never fake code), `Explain` (the plain-English document, request + "Cyrus looked at these images", safety, failure details), `Versions` + `DiffView`, `Composer` (rotating neon rim on focus / listening, images, voice with waveform, model picker Katara / Saka / Yakko with spend meter, game + version picker, estimate).
20880:**v4: the owner's concept (2026-10-07, same branch; replaces v3's look).** Concept: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v4/owner-concept.png`; log + side-by-sides: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v4/` (ROUNDS.md, compare/, best/). Cyrus fills the content area of the normal portal frame (the portal's own sidebar and top bar stay; an earlier "immersive" redraw of the portal chrome was reverted on the owner's call). Inside Cyrus, a top-left **switcher** (`components/cyrus/Switcher.tsx`) holds the projects per game (registry), Custom Project (template library) and the Cyrus Pro card (an upgrade CTA that explains Pro arrives with the token plans), plus Find (P) and New (N). Cyrus does not bind Ctrl K (the portal palette owns it). **The web** is a new engine: `web/tree-layout.ts` (pure, tested) lays out Cyrus core -> game (registry, Minecraft live, ARK / The Isle / Palworld / Rust / Valheim soon, + Add Game) -> category (`lib/cyrus/categories.ts`, deterministic keyword classifier with an "Other" fallback) -> mods (the user's projects, 3 per category + "+N more"; empty categories show templates marked TEMPLATE and a "New … mod" chip that prefills the composer); `web/tree.ts` draws the deep-navy space, drifting aurora ribbons, stars, the neon threads (per-branch hues, S-curves, beads) and travelling light (ambient trickle, brighter on the selected branch, streaming on running builds and on real build events), and moves a DOM layer of real buttons (`Stage.tsx`). **Inspector** (`Inspector.tsx`): Share (copies the link), more menu (jar, source zip, duplicate, copy request, stop), Deploy Mod (= the install modal); tabs Code (path + file switcher + live/final source) / Explain / Versions / Files (folders relative to the plugin package) / Notes; the mod card (category cube, title, version + loader chips, description or the live build stage track, failure verdict with retry, Open Project = zoom to the mod + Files, Download, View on NxLabs disabled until publishing exists) and Related Files. **Composer**: Chat / Generate / Debug / Refactor / Docs; Generate starts a new mod, the others build the next version of the selected mod with the request framed for the mode (`frameRequest` in Composer.tsx); attach, screenshot (getDisplayMedia, one frame), voice, Katara / Saka / Yakko. No "web search" toggle (the builder has no web access). **Icons** (`icons.tsx`): one set, Lucide geometry (ISC notice in the file) drawn with neon gradient strokes + glow (`tone`), original game emblems (NOT official logos: pixel grass cube, stylised A, raptor head, fox-like creature, bolted plate, V rune), isometric category-tinted mod cubes, and the real Nxeon X as the Cyrus mark. Colours are eyedropped from the concept (teal #3ce4dd, magenta-violet #cd4aff, violet #b81afa, cyan #2ed8ec, electric blue #0770fe -> #571af9 core, navy ground #020719) and the threads render as additive bloom (halo + glow + saturated line + white core) with white-cored beads. Light theme: the space canvas stays dark (the concept is neon in space); the switcher, inspector, composer and modals turn light.
20908:- **Preview panel.** Expand/collapse (button, `E`; `Esc` collapses first), stored as `panelWide`; desktop = most of the stage with the dock below, phone = full-screen sheet. Tabs: Code, **Explain**, Files, Versions, Notes. Explain (`preview/ExplainTab.tsx`, `lib/cyrus/explain.ts`) restores v4b: plain English, how to use, commands, settings, permissions, safety scan, limits, the request + attachment thumbnails, and for failed builds the reason, tips, compiler output, **Try again / Edit and retry** (`lib/cyrus/retry.ts`). Template mods get a generated explanation labelled "Template preview". Versions has **Compare** (`preview/CompareView.tsx`, `lib/cyrus/diff.ts`). Header: rename in place (PATCH `title`), favourite, copy link.
20914:### Cyrus v6: broad-request routing, universal categories, listing dialog (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v6-routing`)
20916:**Routing (`lib/cyrus/route.ts`, pure, client-side, zero API calls).** `routeRequest(text, { selection, hover }, { games, projects })` returns a `RouteDecision { intent: create|refine|fix|explain|install|browse|unknown, gameId, categoryId, projectId?, confidence, reason, clarify?, unsupported?, via }`. Fast path only: game names/aliases (typo-tolerant: no typos under 5 letters so "trust" is never Rust, 1 up to 7, 2 beyond; aliases after the first two count as weak content words), `my|the <name> mod/plugin` fuzzy-matched against the account's own projects (plugin names count, "coinshop" = "Coin Shop", version suffixes ignored so "Frost Axe" vs "Frost Axe v2" is a tie), implicit title matches only with an action verb, intent verbs, universal category keywords. The selected (or hovered) mod/game is the context unless the text names another game or asks for a new mod. Ambiguity never calls a model: it returns `clarify` with one-tap options (which game, which mod, "no mod called X: did you mean…"), each a complete decision. Unsupported games (Skyrim, ARK, GTA, Bedrock…) are named plainly with the supported games offered. 80+ phrases in `test/cyrus-route.test.ts`; ~0.1 ms per call. `browse` is an addition to the brief's intents ("what mods do I have for Valheim").
20917:**The dock** (`components/cyrus/prompt/{routing.ts,RouteChip.tsx}`, small hooks into `PromptDock`): the chip shows where the request goes while typing ("Creating a new Minecraft mod in Weapons", "Refining Coin Shop"); Enter acts: create = select game+category then forge, refine/fix = select the mod (camera glides, preview opens) then forge, explain = open the mod's notes (`EXPLAIN_TAB`, switch to studio-ui's Explain tab on merge), install = open the install modal (`cyrus:install` window event, `PreviewPanel` listens), browse = the game's overview. The real/template label and the token estimate follow the decision. Hover isn't wired yet (Network keeps it internally; `RouteContext.hover` is ready).
20919:**Universal categories (`lib/cyrus/categories.ts`).** 16 stable ids, identical on every game: environment, creatures (Creatures & NPCs), weapons, items, magic, vehicles, gameplay, quests, minigames (Game modes), economy, admin, utility (Utility & QoL), interface, visuals, audio, performance. Each has label, blurb, accent, keywords, `store` (the NxLabs TaxKey it files under), `engine` (the template generator archetype) and `worldContent` (could disabling it remove world content, for the lifecycle/toggle policy). `normalizeCategory()` accepts every older id (v5 `worlds/characters/mechanics/shaders`, v4 `worldgen/biomes/structures/other`, plain words). Per game: `categoriesForGame(id, support?)` = the game's `GameSupport.categories` when present, else `DEFAULT_GAME_CATEGORIES`. `CategoryKey` in `lib/cyrus/types.ts` is unchanged: it is now explicitly the generators' archetype; the map/`Mod`/`Selection`/`Game.categories`/route events use `CyrusCategoryId`, and `lib/cyrus/data.ts engineMeta(id, text)` hands a generator its archetype labelled with the universal name. Icons: `components/cyrus/icons/CategoryIcons.tsx` (12 v5 glyphs re-used, 5 new: game modes, economy, admin, utility, performance; 24 px, `currentColor`, 1.6 stroke, duotone).
21010:- **Builds** (`/admin/cyrus/builds`, `/admin/cyrus/builds/<id>`): search by id, plugin, prompt or customer email; filter by outcome, model, game, period. Detail: prompt and change request, stages and events, AI calls (internal model names and cost), usage per stage (live from the service, 0.5+ only), safety findings, files, token hold / charge / refund and ledger rows, the project's versions. Actions: **cancel** (service cancel; "force" fails it locally when the builder is unreachable, then the normal settle runs), **refund tokens** (`creditTokens` kind `refund`, idempotent key `admin-refund:<buildId>`, at most what the build was charged, one per build) and **undo refund** (`revokeTokens` limited to that refund's lot, never below zero), **re-run** (the same request through `createModBuild` for the customer: a real build with AI cost and a normal token hold, confirm box required).
21193:- **Plan estimates** ("about N typical mods or M edits"): `planCapacity(tokens, models, reserve, changeFactor)`. Typical mods = tokens / the *standard* range; edits = tokens / (the *simple* range x the studio's change-request factor, read from `lib/cyrus/estimate.ts`). Shown as a range and labelled an estimate. If the studio's own plan estimator (studio-ui branch) lands as a shared helper, switch the loader to it so both print the same numbers.
21536:**B2 — updates, history, rollback.** `getModsOverview` adds `cyrus` to each Cyrus row (`lib/cyrus-mods/installed.ts`: installed vs current version, labels like `v2 · 1.1.0`, update available, version count, page slug) and sets `availableVersion` from the chain (so the update badge and the Updates count include it). The **Versions** dialog (`mods/CyrusVersions.tsx`, actions in `lib/actions-cyrus-installed.ts`) lists every finished version newest first with its release notes (the builder's own "what changed", else the change request), marks "On this server" / "Latest", offers **Update to latest** and **Roll back to this** (confirm step; one engine `update` job with `targetVersionId`; the replaced jar is backed up). "Latest" = the creator's restored head in Cyrus (`cyrus.headBuildId`) when set, else the newest success. Two versions with the same version string get a distinct package version (`1.1.0+<id6>`), so the engine's idempotency check can't skip a real switch.
21545:- **Build on this mod** (`forkCyrusMod`): the creator just opens their version in Cyrus. Anyone else (who has Cyrus access) gets their OWN copy of the chosen published version: a new succeeded `ModBuild` (jar copied, docs copied, title "<name> (fork)") + `CyrusFork{buildId, sourceBuildId, sourcePageId}`; their copy gets its own private page with "forked from". Change requests on the copy are sent to the build service with the ORIGINAL build as base (`serviceBuildId()` in `app/api/mod-builder/builds` POST, `/source`, `/source-zip`), because the service only knows the original. Forks of forks resolve to the original.
21638:**Remix ("Remix in my Cyrus").** `remixCyrusMod(slug, buildId?)` replaces the old fork path (`forkCyrusMod` now delegates to it). Rules (`remixDecision`): signed in, has Cyrus access, page PUBLIC and not hidden, creator's remix setting **OPEN (default)**, the version's safety verdict not `block`; the creator just opens their own version. Before anything is copied the code is **re-scanned** (`rescan.ts`): the jar's sha256 must match `ModBuild.jarSha256`, and the build service's source heuristics (a TS port of `services/modbuilder/scan.js scanSource`, plus an API-key check) run over the version's source fetched from the service; a block refuses the remix, a builder outage refuses it too (fail closed). Then: own `ModBuild` copy (title "<name> (remix)", Notes seeded with "Remixed from…" + the original's prompt history, `remixNotes()`), `CyrusFork` (service base id, unchanged) and **`CyrusRemix`** (parent page + exact parent version + origin + depth + the re-scan result). Later change requests on the remix are normal builds (the service scans those in full).
21700:- **`lib/cyrus/games/valheim.ts`** is the `GameSupport` record. It covers the versions (1.0.x current, 0.221.x legacy, older unsupported), where a mod installs and why, breakage risks, outdated signals, the 12 universal categories, sources and unknowns. It also holds `VALHEIM_TARGET`, the one place to bump after a Valheim patch (game line 1.0, network version 40, BepInExPack 5.4.2351, Jötunn 2.30.2, publicizer 0.4.3), plus `valheimModSide()`. That function decides the install side: content mods and smelter automation go on **both** (server and every player, versions enforced), HUD, music, grading and quest/pulse mechanics on **client**.
21721:  Every plugin now sets `Game.isModded = true` (Iron Gate's request; it also disables achievements) and logs a warning when the running game is outside the 1.0 line. Content mods depend on Jötunn and declare `NetworkCompatibility(EveryoneMustHaveMod, Minor)`. Output also includes a Thunderstore-valid `manifest.json`, a `cyrus.json` (target game/network version, side, install note, removal warning, loader pins), AI-disclosure `AssemblyMetadata`, and for Yakko an xUnit project that compiles only the pure balance class (`CYRUS_TESTS`).
21726:Terraria has two separate modding worlds and Cyrus now picks one per request (`terrariaFlavor` in
21829:- **Starter-grant abuse guard** (`lib/cyrus/tokens/starter-guard.ts`): one free build per real person. Alias addresses (dots, +tags, googlemail) share one grant (dedupe via the ledger idempotency key on a hash of the normalized email); throwaway-inbox domains get none (they can still buy tokens). The disposable list is a baseline: extend it from real abuse. Per-IP/device caps are not built yet (need request context + storage).
21933:**What remains before the real installer can be switched on** (not done, deliberately): (1) call it from a worker job under the per-server lock (a new job type or a step in `GAME_MOD_SYNC`) with an `open` that uses `SshGuestFs` (or `LocalGuestFs` in SANDBOX), never from a request handler; (2) put the built jar at `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGIN_DIR/nxeon-pack-loader/NxeonPackLoader-0.1.0.jar` on the worker host; (3) decide how the Mods tab treats the engine-state root `managed:<key>` (it has no GameMod row: today it would not be listed, and nothing stops a customer deleting the jar by hand) and hook `canUserRemove` into any removal path; (4) order it before the dependent Cyrus mod's install and release it after uninstall; (5) a restart is needed for a newly placed plugin (engine `restartRequired`); (6) the engine never deletes `plugins/NxeonPackLoader/` (packs.json, telemetry.json) on uninstall, by design (only files it placed).

content.thinking:
That's a lot of icons to cover, so I'll build a template-driven generator instead of drawing each one individually: a small set of base shapes (ingots, gems, tools, armor pieces, food items) that I can recolor and vary to produce the full icon set efficiently.

Then I'm sketching out Screen 3, the Mod Packs + Conflict report page, with breadcrumb navigation, a server selector chip, and a left column member list for picking which mods to include in the pack.

I'm also planning a server inventory panel showing a read-only scan of the server: Paper version, plugin count with examples like EssentialsX and LuckPerms, datapacks, resource pack ownership, and detection of Geyser/Floodgate.

In the center, I'm designing a conflict report panel that counts findings by severity (blocking, warn, info, not checked), with sortable cards showing evidence, affected mods, and a resolution proposal with buttons to apply, decide manually, or acknowledge — including an example of a blocking dependency conflict involving Void Arsenal's soft dependency.

For the realistic blocking case, I'm settling on a `platform.api_version` conflict: Banshee Hunt declares API 26.2 but the server runs 1.21.11, so the resolution proposes rebuilding the mod to target 1.21.11.

I'm also adding a `command.label_collision` warning — a third Cyrus mod, "Market Stalls," conflicts with ShopGUIPlus over the `/shop` command, resolved by aliasing it to a namespaced label like `/m4rkshop`.

Then there's a resource pack ownership warning since ItemsAdder already owns a pack and we're adding another, an event overlap note for PlayerDeathEvent between Banshee Hunt and EssentialsX resolved by load order, and auto-resolved stacking warnings for whole-file resource pack merges. I'm also logging info-level notices for sounds.json, lang file, and datapack function tag merges, plus a collapsed section for pre-existing server problems that shouldn't block anything.

I'm compiling the "not checked" items too — things like event overlap needing a player to be observable, undeclared entity budgets estimated from bytecode, and ShopGUIPlus classes skipped for being too large. Then on the composed pack side, I'm summarizing the nxpack.json output: pack ID, version bump from 1.2.4 to 1.3.0, four members (three embedded, one by reference), merged resource pack mode at 1.8 MB, and the changelog of added/removed/updated entries, followed by per-version test rows starting with 1.21.11 showing a blocked static check and a dynamic run that didn't count as a pass.

After resolving that, static checks come back with warnings and dynamic stays not_run, with a "Run Test Flight" button planned to trigger a combined boot plus differential boots per changed member. I'm wrestling with how to show evidence honestly — defaulting to a not-run state and offering a clearly labeled "ILLUSTRATIVE STATE" toggle rather than faking real results, since showing illustrative data as long as it's labeled is acceptable but presenting fake data as real isn't. For installing as one unit, I'm laying out the step sequence: validate, fetch and verify, publish the resource pack, preflight, snapshot for backup, remove dropped items, place, update Pack Loader entries, record the unit, and verify — emphasizing that every touched path gets snapshotted with verified checksums.

Backups get deleted only after a confirmed successful install, and any failure restores the exact original bytes; the install button stays disabled until blocking issues are cleared, and rollback is framed as simply installing a prior version's manifest. Since real installs are currently gated behind a feature flag, I'm deciding to phrase that for customers as "Installing packs isn't switched on yet" rather than exposing flag internals, while keeping technical notes in an owner-only tooltip. Now I'm moving to the mod import screen, thinking through whether to use a stepper layout (Upload, Ownership, Detected, Scan, Revision 0, then collaborative work) as a single flowing page or a page with a persistent left-side stepper, leaning toward a completed-summary view with sections for review purposes.

For the upload card I'm detailing drop-zone support for source ZIP, plugin JAR, data pack ZIP, and resource pack ZIP (25 MB cap), a sample uploaded file with its hash, a list of passed ingestion checks (file count, compression ratio, symlinks, nesting depth), and a note that build files like build.gradle or gradlew are read only for detection and never executed. In the center I'm laying out the ownership attestation card with a checkbox, typed name, and versioned attestation ID, plus a separate optional sharing-consent flow that checks license files (e.g., MIT) to determine whether sharing is permitted, defaulting to private if the license is unknown. Then I'm specifying the detected-framework section showing a Paper plugin, Gradle build system (detected but not executed), Java 21 targeting two version options, and the project name and version.

I'm continuing the detection details with the main class, API version, commands, permissions, and dependency checks — placeholderapi and vault-api passing the allowlist, while bStats is explicitly refused as a direct dependency (requiring the Metrics class to be copied into source instead). I'm also wiring up mock toggles for unsupported states like Kotlin or a non-allowlisted dependency such as WorldEdit, and building the scan result panel that always reports a "warn" verdict (never "safe") with specific fixture warnings around reflection and network calls tied to Metrics, UpdateChecker, and known endpoints — while asserting that Cyrus itself will never add networking, reflection, or database access to the codebase. I'm pausing on whether labeling these as results from a real run on node-2 might read as misleading to the project owner.

Now I'm making sure the sample page is clearly marked as a demo, naming it ImportDemo and labeling it "Sample: the import test fixture" so it's unmistakable to the owner. I'm laying out the right column with a Revision 0 card showing import details — ModSpec derived from plugin.yml, compile time, jar size, reproducibility, and namespace rules for new identifiers — plus a "Test Flight: not run yet" button and a "Work on it with Cyrus" prompt dock with a route chip, input field, model selector, and token estimate, along with a note that imported README/LICENSE content is always treated as quoted data rather than instructions. I'm also defining the jar-only state, where Cyrus can only analyze and check conflicts but can't rebuild the jar, disabling the prompt dock accordingly. Then I'm moving on to sketch out Screen 5, the Data Pack and Worldgen studio, starting with its breadcrumb trail and layout structure.

Now I'm fleshing out the left-hand resource tree for the data pack studio, grouping items into Recipes, Loot tables, Advancements, Tags, Functions, Enchantments, and a separate Worldgen section covering dimension types, dimensions, biomes, features, and structures. I'm deciding to build a cohesive "frostlands" namespace sample with concrete showcase content — a frost sword recipe, a ruin chest loot table, a frostbite enchantment, hello/tick functions, and worldgen elements like frozen biomes, ore and tree features, and a ruin structure template — then sketching the center panel as a typed form editor, defaulting to the frozen_reach biome with fields for temperature, downfall, precipitation, and color swatches.

I'm also planning a per-version status header showing Generated/Validated/Loaded badges across six target versions, being honest that this sample pack hasn't actually been flight-tested, plus a toggle between the form view and emitted JSON so switching target versions visibly changes the output format (e.g., int colors vs hex strings, effects vs attributes for 1.21.11+). For functions, I'm designing a safety panel that checks each command line against allowed roots, flags risky ones like `op @a`, warns on `summon` inside tick functions, and enforces a command budget and call-graph depth limit.

For structure templates, I'm sketching a dedicated block-layout editor with a layer slider, a 7x7 grid using single-character palette entries, and an isometric preview canvas, which takes over the center panel when that resource type is selected. I'm also adding an honest banner for worldgen resources noting that a restart is required, only new chunks get it, and the dimension must be reached via a specific teleport command rather than a portal. The right column will house tabbed Checks (spec and file-level validations) and a Cost estimate panel for worldgen-heavy resources.

I'll compute the cost estimate using a plausible heuristic formula based on terrain and biome feature load, labeling it clearly as an estimate rather than exact. For screenshots, I'll default to the biome form but also capture the structure editor and function safety states, plus narrow-view review-and-approve cards similar to the texture workflow. Given the scope, I'll start building the kit now, reusing common.css as a base to save effort.

"""Inline v2/src/<page>.html + css + js + fonts + images into self-contained mockups in v2/ (no network)."""
import base64, re, os, sys
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))); S = os.path.join(D, "src")
PAGES = ["item-designer.html", "menu-quest.html", "mod-packs.html", "import-mod.html", "datapack-studio.html"]

cache = {}
def data(rel):
    p = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(S, rel))
    if p not in cache: cache[p] = f"data:{MIME[os.path.splitext(p)[1]]};base64," + base64.b64encode(open(p, "rb").read()).decode()
    return cache[p]
def assets(t): return re.sub(r"\.\./assets/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.(?:webp|png|svg|woff2)", lambda m: data(m.group(0)), t)

There are still problems: the left column panels overlap because flex children shrink inside scroll containers, so I need to force those panels to not shrink. The graph is still getting cut off, the sim timeline is too cramped at 70px, the node/depth text wraps awkwardly, and the recipe arrow needs fixing too.

The core issue is too much crammed into the center column. I'm deciding to move the simulator into the right column as its own tab alongside Parameters and Checks, giving the center column full height for the graph, and sizing the sim tab's buttons, timeline, and log list to fit within roughly 420px. I'll shoot screenshots of both the Parameters tab and a Simulator tab since the brief calls out both features as important. I also want to shorten the trigger block description from four lines down to something like "Charge and release" with a tooltip. Implementation-wise, I'm moving the sim rendering into a new right-tab pane and keeping the pending box visible only on the params tab.

# Cyrus studios v2: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files: `item-designer.html`, `menu-quest.html` (tabs Menus / Quests), `mod-packs.html`, `import-mod.html`, `datapack-studio.html`. Self-contained, no network. Sources `src/` (`kit.css`/`kit.js` = the approved v1 kit, `v2.css`/`ext.js` = shell + shared pieces), build `tools/build.py`, shots `tools/run-shots.sh` (node-2, capped slice) into `shots/` (28 PNGs). Query params pick review states; `ctl=0` hides the dashed mockup bar.

## Principles
- **One product.** The shell copies the shipped studio (impl-shots/texture-*): the real portal sidebar and top bar, the Cyrus bar (wordmark, crumbs, context switch, Mod assets, token chip, theme), glass panels with mono eyebrows, the inspector tab anatomy, the conic-rim prompt dock at the bottom of the centre column.
- **One accent.** Violet means selected or primary. Cyan only means "now" (the simulator playhead). Green, amber, red only mean pass, warn, fail/blocking.
- **Typed, never node soup.** Graphs are columns (When, Only if, Do) with nested containers for loops; every block shows its config path (`a0.n1`).
- **Caps are budgets.** Every limit is a meter or a counter (`20/64 actions`, `3/16 biomes`, `214/2048 progress chars`), and an overrun shows the validator's own code and message.
- **Honesty.** Real-client gameplay is "not verified" everywhere. "Not run" is never a pass. Sample content is labelled. The one illustrative Test Flight result carries an "Illustrative: nothing was run" banner. The attested scan never says safe.

## Mapping to backend data
| Screen | Data and caps |
|---|---|
| Item Designer | `ItemDesign` v1 (the Void Reaper fixture verbatim). Budget meters = `budgetOf()` ported 1:1 vs `BUDGET` (64/32/8/512/3), nodes 48, depth 3, 16 actions per list. Gate column = the `Ability` protocol (re-entry, cooldown, charges, conditions). Parameters = `params.ts` paths (`items.void_reaper.abilities.void_pull.a0.radius`) with `CAPS` ranges; saving shows "config.yml only, config_version 1→2, 27 Java files unchanged". Structure fields name the one Java file they rebuild. Simulator = `simulate.ts` semantics: charge = held/max, per-owner mark cap with oldest replaced, feedback text on cooldown. Asset chips run `canAsset` (texture top plan, sound Saka+). |
| Menus | `MenuDesign` chest (shop fixture: 6 rows, 28 list slots, 30 config entries, prev/next 48/50). Cost types item / xp_levels / economy; the CostCharger order room → pay → take → give drives "Try it". Checks use real codes (`economy_needs_vault`, `cost_loop`, `arbitrage_loop`, `slot_overlap`). |
| Quests | `QuestDesign` (trial_one/two/three, daily_bread fixtures): requires, branches (max 3), repeat daily, objectives with counts, rewards (max 8), stored-progress size from `progressEntryChars`. Backend is in progress (feature/cyrus-r11, uncommitted). |
| Mod Packs | Inventory (`scanServer`, redacted keys counted), findings with the engine's class/severity/resolution table, server-only findings separated, `notChecked` listed, `nxpack.json` summary (merged pack, `required: false`, changelog), compatibility row (static / boot, `not_run`), dynamic plan (1 combined + differential boots), the unit install steps and backup lifetime. Install off: `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL`. |
| Import | ImportDemo fixture: ingestion caps, build files read-not-run, attestation + share consent with the text-version ids, SPDX detection, the allowlist (placeholderapi, vault-api), `unsupported: X`, the attested profile's 5 real warnings, revision 0 facts from the node-2 run, token estimate from the reserve table (Saka standard 60–220). Jar = analysis only, dock disabled. |
| Data packs + worldgen | DataPackSpec v1 resource kinds and pack caps, six pinned versions, per-version emitted JSON (attributes + `#rrggbb` from 1.21.11, music list from 1.21.4, carvers map on 1.21.1), the function allowlist and refusals (live "Try a command"), function limits, the template layout spec (palette chars, `.` void, 48³, 32768 blocks, 16 loot containers), the cost heuristic and per-class recommendation, the restart / new-chunks banner. |

## Component inventory (React)
- `StudioShell` (existing) + `DesignerSwitch({kind: items|menus|quests})`, `TargetVersionChip`.
- `BudgetMeter({label, used, cap})`, `IssueList({issues})` (code, path, message, severity), `CheckList` (reuse `QualityPanel`).
- Item: `ItemHeader`, `AssetRefChip({kind, key, decision})`, `AbilityGraph({ability, selected})` → `TriggerBlock`, `GateChain`, `ActionBlock`, `LoopContainer`; `ParamField({path, value, cap, changed})`, `ParamsPanel`, `PendingEditBar({edits, files, configVersion})`, `DesignSimulator({design, events})`, `DisplayContextPreview` (reuse the shipped In game view), `DesignDock` (parameter-request preview).
- Menu: `SlotGrid({rows, slots, list, page, mode})`, `Slot`, `SlotInspector`, `ClickProtocol({steps})`, `ConfigListTable`. Quest: `QuestChain`, `QuestFlow` → `StepCard`, `ObjectiveRow`, `BranchColumns`, `RewardChips`; `QuestSimulator`.
- Packs: `MemberList`, `InventorySummary`, `FindingCard({finding, onResolve})`, `ManifestSummary`, `CompatRow`, `UnitInstallCard`.
- Import: `UploadKinds`, `IngestChecklist`, `AttestationForm`, `DetectedFacts`, `DependencyRow({state})`, `AttestedScan`, `RevisionZeroCard`.
- Data packs: `ResourceTree`, `VersionStatusRow`, `BiomeForm` (+ one form per kind), `EmittedJson({version})`, `TemplateEditor({layers, palette})`, `IsoPreview`, `FunctionSafety`, `WorldgenCost`, `RestartBanner`.
- `PixelIcon` (sample art; see question 1).

## Interaction details
- Graph and Parameters edit the same value; a block click highlights its settings. Changed values show the old value struck through.
- Menus: Edit selects slots (numbers on hover); Try it buys with a sample inventory and shows each protocol step; arrows page the list.
- Quests: chain cards select a quest; player events advance the simulator; +24 h re-opens the daily.
- Packs: Apply / Acknowledge / Undo per finding; Install stays disabled while anything blocks; Run Test Flight is disabled while blocked.
- Data packs: the target version changes JSON and checks; paint template cells with the selected palette char; layers above the current one dim in the preview.
- Narrow (< 760 px): read-only summary plus Approve / Reject on every screen.

## Accessibility
Focus rings from the kit; status always has text, not colour alone; checkboxes have `role="checkbox"` and `aria-checked`; required fields are `aria-required`; MC-coloured names sit on a dark chip in light mode for contrast; reduced motion stops the glint and the dock rim. Open: keyboard painting for the slot grid and template cells, screen-reader summaries of the graph and the timeline.

## Deliberately excluded
Free-form node wiring, custom code blocks (`run_command` does not exist), dialogue-menu editor (listed, not drawn), forms for every resource kind (the biome, the template and the functions are drawn), creatures and RigSpec (no screen requested), real vanilla item art, prices, invented Test Flight results (one illustrative state, labelled).

## Open questions for the owner
1. **Item icons.** The mockups use pixel icons drawn here. Production needs a source: our own icon set, or icons rendered from the client's assets (licence check)?
2. Should settings-only edits skip the model and cost 0 tokens (`planDesignEdit` is built, not wired)?
3. Menu and quest designers are still in progress on feature/cyrus-r11. Are dialogue menus and the 8-menu / 16-quest limits the scope you want?
4. Can a Mod Pack install while user-decision warnings are open (today: yes, unless acknowledgement is required)?
5. Third-party members: search Modrinth/Hangar, or paste a link? The download allow-list isn't wired.
6. Worldgen restart: automatic after install, or confirmed by the customer? On uninstall, keep or archive the dimension folders?
7. Are "Try it" and the quest simulator customer-facing, or creator-only?
8. The approve flows on mobile: allowed, or view-only (open from v1)?
9. Attestation and share-consent wording: approve the texts shown?
